children: is in the spotlight after one of the bluest of the blue chips reported third-quarter earnings results. In general, analysts have not been pushed off their bull ratings on the beverage stock.
Jefferies Kaumil Gajrawala thinks the strong Coca-Cola

report will be enough to keep the bull thesis alive. He noted that organic sales topped expectations by a wide margin (+7% vs. +2% consensus) even when accounting for timing. While the KO trade was noted to be a crowded long near all-time highs and elevated valuation, Gajrawala and his team think earnings expectations are still going up and that the gap between Coke and peers is widening. "Importantly, case volumes remained strong post-World Cup (+5%). As the market debates price increases, those delivering volume growth should outperform," he advised. Reiterate Buy.
Bank of America analyst Peter Galbo said even though expectations were elevated heading into the earnings print, Coca-Cola's
underlying results are strong enough for shares to react favorably. Galbo on his team latched on to Coca-Cola's
raised organic sales and EPS growth guidance, as well as the expected tailwinds from F/X and M&A,
Morgan Stanley analyst Eric Serotta called Coca-Cola's
results impressive but unsurprising in comparison to investor expectations. The earnings update was said to confirm the firm's view that Coca-Cola's
organic sales growth is sustainably above mega-cap peers, with strong pricing power, consistent share gains, strong Fairlife growth, and a consistent competitive advantage all working in its favor.
showed a 0.5% decline at 11:55 a.m. after bouncing back and forth between positive and negative territory.
